microcopy.what: An exploratory literature brief is a bounded, orienting look at a topic's existing literature -- a prior-work check or a related-work draft for a reviewer who is not running a formal evidence-synthesis review at all.
microcopy.gives: A relevance-tagged reading of the candidates a bounded search across enabled connectors turned up, a corpus-description table, a landscape brief, an optional related-work draft, and a supplementary search log -- never a PRISMA flow diagram or an eligibility-screened study set, because this method never runs formal eligibility screening.
microcopy.costs: Typically hours to a few days; one reviewer is normal and never disclosed as a shortfall, because this method has no reviewer-count conduct floor to fall short of.
microcopy.cannot_claim: That prior work does not exist, that the search reached saturation, that records were screened or found eligible/ineligible against criteria, or that anything here is a systematic or scoping review -- the label is unconditional and never upgrades on its own.

stage_names.extract: tag each candidate's relevance facets and draft prior-work claims with provenance
stage_names.appraise: not applicable -- this method does no formal quality appraisal
stage_names.synthesize: not applicable -- no pooling or structured synthesis family applies
stage_names.report: draft the landscape brief (and, optionally, a related-work section and a supplementary search log)
